mainTopic: The meaning of אמן, generous readings of harsh פסוקים, how few are redeemed, משה's complaint and punishment, and משה's lesson about ארך אפים.
overview: The גמרא opens by explaining that the word אמן stands for אל מלך נאמן, 'God, faithful King.' Next, ריש לקיש gives harsh readings of three פסוקים about who will be saved. Each time רבי יוחנן answers, 'Their Master is not pleased that you said this about them,' and offers a kinder reading. רב later corrects his student רב כהנא in the same words. רב then teaches him that Torah is not found in someone who keeps himself comfortable while learning. A ברייתא teaches that only a small share left מצרים, and רבא says the days of משיח will be the same. Another ברייתא tells how משה was punished for complaining about the people's suffering. הקדוש ברוך הוא contrasts him with אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, who never questioned Him, and tells משה he will not see the conquest of ארץ ישראל. Finally, the גמרא asks what משה saw when he hurried to bow. One answer is ארך אפים, and a ברייתא tells how משה once said the wicked should be lost. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does the word אמן mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word אמן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'אמן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the meaning of the word אמן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמן is a word everyone says after a ברכה. The גמרא wants to know if it carries a deeper meaning beyond just 'yes' or 'true'.

keyTerms.meaning: Amen, the word said in reply to a ברכה

phrases.english: What is 'Amen'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new short topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning hidden in the word אמן.

steps.title: אמן stands for God, faithful King
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that אמן is made from the first letters of אל מלך נאמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: It stands for 'God, faithful King.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question. The three letters of אמן are the first letters of three words: אל, מלך, נאמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So saying אמן is not just agreeing. It also declares that God is a King who can be trusted.
steps.whatToRemember: אמן = אל מלך נאמן, 'God, faithful King.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
'God, faithful King.'
phrases.notes: Look at the first letter of each word: א, מ, נ. Together they spell אמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמן is made of the first letters of אל מלך נאמן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: missing even one law opens the netherworld
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the פסוק 'the netherworld opened its mouth without law' as being about someone who leaves out even one law.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Therefore the netherworld has enlarged itself and opened its mouth without measure (law).' ריש לקיש said: This is for someone who leaves out even one law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ישעיהו, and ריש לקיש gives a strict reading of it. Anyone who fails to keep even one law is at risk of the netherworld.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words לבלי חק can mean 'for lacking a law.' ריש לקיש reads it as lacking even a single law, which is a very high bar. This sets up the first of three disagreements with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The netherworld, the place of punishment
Without measure / for lacking a law

phrases.english: 'Therefore the netherworld has enlarged itself'
'and opened its mouth without measure.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:14. The word חֹק can mean 'measure' or 'law,' and the reading below depends on 'law.'

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
For one who leaves out even one law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: harsh versus generous readings of פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The netherworld opens for anyone who leaves out even one law.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even one law learned is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's harsh reading and says the פסוק is only about someone who did not learn even one law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Their Master is not pleased that you said this about them. Rather, it means that even if a person learned only one law, he is saved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back on ריש לקיש. He says God would not want the Jewish people described so harshly, and he flips the reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריש לקיש's reading, almost everyone would be doomed, since nearly no one keeps every law. רבי יוחנן reads 'without law' as a person with no laws at all. Anyone who learned even one is safe.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Their Master' does not mean a human teacher. It is a respectful way of saying God, the Master of the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is not pleasing to their Master
that you say this about them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לֹא לָמַד אֶלָּא חוֹק אֶחָד.
phrases.english: rather, even if he learned only one law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִיחָא לְמָרַיְיהוּ דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the strict reading of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole strict reading of לבלי חק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It speaks too harshly of the Jewish people, which God does not want.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only a third of שם's descendants survive
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק that two parts will die and a third will remain, ריש לקיש says it means a third of the descendants of שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'In all the land, says God, two parts will be cut off and die, and the third will remain.' ריש לקיש said: A third of the descendants of שם.
steps.whatsHappening: A second פסוק, from זכריה, and again ריש לקיש reads it strictly. Only one third of the descendants of שם will survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Limiting the survivors to a third of שם's descendants means most of the world is destroyed. This sets up רבי יוחנן's second answer.

phrases.english: (As it says:) 'And in all the land, says God,'
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: 'two parts of it will be cut off and die,'
'and the third will remain in it.'
phrases.notes: זכריה 13:8

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A third of Shem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: שְׁלִישִׁי שֶׁל שֵׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a third of שם's descendants will remain.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a third of all נח's descendants
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן again objects and says the third that survives is a third of all of נח's descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Their Master is not pleased that you said this about them. Rather, even a third of נח's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן uses the same line again and widens the circle. The surviving third is counted from all of humanity, the descendants of נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all people come from נח, a third of נח's descendants is far more people than a third of שם's. רבי יוחנן's reading saves many more.

keyTerms.meaning: נח, ancestor of all people after the flood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
It is not pleasing to their Master
that you say this about them,
rather, even a third of Noah.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִיחָא לְמָרַיְיהוּ דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the strict reading of step 5.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Counting only from שם is too harsh.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: one from a city means just one
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'I will take one from a city and two from a family,' ריש לקיש says to read it literally.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For I have taken you to Me, and I will take you one from a city and two from a family.' ריש לקיש said: The words mean exactly what they say.
steps.whatsHappening: A third פסוק, from ירמיהו. ריש לקיש says only one person per city and two per family will be taken in the redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the redemption saves just a few scattered people. This sets up רבי יוחנן's third answer.

keyTerms.meaning: I have taken you to Me (as a husband)
The words mean exactly as written

phrases.english: 'For I have taken you to Myself,'
'and I will take you, one from a city'
'and two from a family.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:14

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The words are as they are written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third example of the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one per city and two per family will be redeemed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one person's merit saves the whole city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says one righteous person brings merit to the whole city, and two bring merit to the whole family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Their Master is not pleased that you said this about them. Rather, one from a city brings merit to the entire city, and two from a family bring merit to the entire family.
steps.whatsHappening: For the third time רבי יוחנן objects with the same line. He reads 'one from a city' as one person whose merit saves everyone in the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש counted only the survivors. רבי יוחנן makes those few people the cause of everyone else being saved, through their זכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings merit to, causes to be saved

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
It is not pleasing to their Master
that you say this about them,
rather, one from a city
brings merit to the entire city,
and two from a family
bring merit to the entire family.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְמָרַיְיהוּ דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the literal reading of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The literal reading of 'one from a city.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leaves almost everyone unsaved, which God does not want said.

steps.title: רב כהנא gives the same literal reading before רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רב כהנא, sitting before רב, also said the פסוק means just what it says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא sat before רב, and he sat and said: The words are as they are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where the same argument happened in another generation. רב כהנא gave ריש לקיש's literal reading in front of his teacher רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the literal reading was not only ריש לקיש's view. It sets up רב's answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana sat before Rav
and sat and said:
The words are as they are written.
phrases.notes: This is about the same פסוק from ירמיהו in step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the reading of step 7 in a new setting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק means only one per city and two per family.

steps.title: רב answers just like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects רב כהנא's reading with the same words רבי יוחנן used: one person's merit saves the whole city and family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: Their Master is not pleased that you said this about them. Rather, one from a city brings merit to the whole city, and two from a family bring merit to the whole family.
steps.whatsHappening: רב corrects his student exactly the way רבי יוחנן corrected ריש לקיש. The kind reading is confirmed by a second great teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate authorities, רבי יוחנן and רב, say the same thing in the same words. That makes the generous reading the clear conclusion of this section.

keyTerms.meaning: Merit, the good earned by a righteous person

steps.whatToRemember: Four times the strict reading is rejected with 'Their Master is not pleased that you said this about them.' We should read פסוקים about the Jewish people in the kindest way: even one law learned saves, a third of all humanity survives, and a few righteous people bring merit to their whole city and family.

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
It is not pleasing to their Master
that you say this about them,
rather, one from a city
brings merit to the whole city,
and two from a family
bring merit to the whole family.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב: לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְמָרַיְיהוּ דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב כהנא's reading in step 9, matching רבי יוחנן in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The literal reading of 'one from a city.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It speaks too harshly of the Jewish people.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The few righteous people bring merit to their whole city and family.

steps.title: רב quotes a verse when he sees רב כהנא grooming
steps.stepSummary: רב sees רב כהנא wash his hair before sitting down to learn, and quotes a פסוק from איוב about Torah not being found in the land of the living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב saw that רב כהנא was washing his head, then came up and sat before רב. רב said to him: 'Nor shall it be found in the land of the living.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רב כהנא learning before רב continues. רב quotes a פסוק when he sees רב כהנא caring for his hair before learning. This sets up the next two steps, where רב כהנא reacts and רב explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב is about wisdom, but heard out of context it sounds like a curse: 'you will not be found among the living.' The next step shows that רב כהנא hears it exactly that way.

keyTerms.meaning: before רב, in front of his teacher

phrases.english: He saw him, that he was washing his head
phrases.notes: רב is the one watching, and רב כהנא is the one washing his hair.

phrases.english: and then came up and sat before רב.
He said to him: 'Nor shall it be found in the land of the living.'
phrases.notes: איוב 28:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב כהנא sitting before רב from steps 9 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב applies the פסוק 'Nor shall it be found in the land of the living' to רב כהנא.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks if he is being cursed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא thinks the פסוק was aimed at him as a curse and asks רב about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you cursing me?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא understands the פסוק as a curse and asks רב if that is what he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read on its face, the פסוק means someone will not be found among the living. רב כהנא's question sets up רב's real explanation in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵילָט קָא לָיְיטַתְּ לִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are you cursing me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the פסוק רב quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב's quoting of the פסוק was meant as a curse against רב כהנא.

steps.title: Torah is not found in someone who pampers himself
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that he was only quoting a פסוק. It teaches that Torah is not found in someone who keeps himself comfortable while learning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am saying a verse. Torah will not be found in one who 'keeps himself living' (pampers himself) over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that this was no curse. He was teaching רב כהנא what the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'the land of the living' as a person who 'gives himself life,' meaning comfort and pampering. The lesson is that Torah is acquired through effort and hardship, not through ease. Washing and grooming before learning is the kind of comfort רב is hinting at.

keyTerms.meaning: I am just saying a verse
keeps himself living, meaning he pampers himself

steps.whatToRemember: Torah is not found in someone who keeps himself comfortable while learning it.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am saying a verse,
Torah will not be found
in one who keeps himself living (in comfort) over it.
phrases.notes: This plays on the word חיים in the פסוק: 'living' here means giving yourself an easy, comfortable life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was not a curse. The פסוק teaches that Torah is not found in someone who pampers himself while learning it.

steps.title: Only two of 600,000 left מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רב סימאי compares leaving מצרים to entering ארץ ישראל. Only two of 600,000 entered the land, and only that same share left מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רב סימאי says, it says 'And I will take you to Me as a people,' and it says 'And I will bring you.' The Torah compares their leaving Egypt to their entering the land. Just as when they entered the land it was two out of six hundred thousand, so too when they left Egypt it was two out of six hundred thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings a new teaching about how few people are redeemed. It learns this from two פסוקים that stand next to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים in שמות are placed side by side, so the leaving and the entering are compared. We know that only two of the generation that left entered the land. So the same small share must have left מצרים, and the rest died there.

keyTerms.meaning: compares, linking two things that stand side by side

phrases.english: It was taught: רב סימאי says, it is stated:
'And I will take you to Me as a people,'
phrases.notes: שמות 6:7

phrases.english: and it is stated: 'And I will bring you.'
phrases.notes: שמות 6:8, the next פסוק, which continues 'into the land.'

phrases.english: It compares their leaving Egypt to their entering the land.

phrases.aramaic: מָה בִּיאָתָן לָאָרֶץ – שְׁנַיִם מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא,
phrases.english: Just as their entering the land was two out of six hundred thousand,
phrases.notes: These two are כלב and יהושע, the only ones of that generation who entered the land.

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְצִיאָתָן מִמִּצְרַיִם – שְׁנַיִם מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא.
phrases.english: so too their leaving Egypt was two out of six hundred thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new ברייתא about how few are redeemed, which fits the earlier theme of only a few surviving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only two of 600,000 left מצרים, the same share that entered the land.

steps.title: The days of משיח will be the same
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that the days of משיח will match the leaving of מצרים, so only a few will be redeemed then too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And so too in the days of משיח, as it says: 'And she shall respond there as in the days of her youth, and as on the day she came up from the land of Egypt.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא extends רב סימאי's teaching to the final redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע compares the future redemption to 'the day she came up from Egypt.' Since only a few left מצרים, only a few will be part of the redemption in the days of משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: the days of משיח, the final redemption
and so too, the same rule applies

phrases.english: רבא said: And so too in the days of משיח,
as it is stated: 'And she shall respond there as in the days of her youth,'
phrases.notes: הושע 2:17

phrases.english: 'and as on the day she came up from the land of Egypt.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב סימאי's comparison from step 14 to the days of משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a few will be redeemed in the days of משיח, just as only a few left מצרים.
steps.whatToRemember: Entering the land, leaving מצרים, and the coming of משיח are all compared, and in each only a small share takes part.

steps.title: An old Egyptian describes what his ancestors did
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי tells of meeting an old man in Alexandria. The old man described how the Egyptians drowned, killed, and crushed the Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said, once I came to Alexandria of Egypt. I found an old man who said to me: Come, I will show you what my ancestors did to your ancestors. Some of them they drowned in the sea, some they killed by the sword, and some they crushed in buildings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens with a story about the suffering in מצרים. It sets up the next step, which explains how this suffering connects to משה being punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man lists three kinds of cruelty: drowning, killing by the sword, and crushing inside the walls of buildings. This picture of terrible suffering is the background for משה's complaint in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: It was taught: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי said,

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת נִכְנַסְתִּי לַאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם.
phrases.english: once I entered Alexandria of Egypt.
I found one old man, and he said to me:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וְאַרְאֶךָּ מָה עָשׂוּ אֲבוֹתַי לַאֲבוֹתֶיךָ.
phrases.english: Come and I will show you what my ancestors did to your ancestors.
Some of them they drowned in the sea,
some of them they killed by the sword,
some of them they crushed in the building.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the suffering in מצרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Egyptians drowned, killed, and crushed the Jewish people.

steps.title: משה was punished for complaining about this suffering
steps.stepSummary: Because of this suffering, משה complained to הקדוש ברוך הוא, and he was punished for that complaint.
steps.simpleTranslation: And over this matter משה רבינו was punished, as it says: 'And since I came to פרעה to speak in Your name, he has done evil to this people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא connects the suffering to משה. His protest about it brought him a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה saw that things got worse after he spoke to פרעה, and he questioned הקדוש ברוך הוא. The ברייתא says this complaint was held against him.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נֶעֱנַשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
phrases.english: And over this matter משה our teacher was punished,
phrases.notes: 'This matter' means משה complaining about the suffering, as the פסוק right after shows.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And since I came to Pharaoh'
phrases.notes: שמות 5:23

phrases.english: 'to speak in Your name, he has done evil to this people.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נֶעֱנַשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the suffering described in step 16 to משה's complaint and punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was punished for questioning הקדוש ברוך הוא over the suffering of the people.

steps.title: The אבות never questioned הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא mourns the loss of the אבות. He appeared to them as אל שדי, and they never questioned His ways or asked His name.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: Woe over those who are lost and can no longer be found! Many times I revealed Myself to אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב as אל שדי, and they did not question My ways, and they did not say to Me 'What is Your name?'
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers משה by contrasting him with the אבות, who trusted Him without complaint. This sets up the examples that follow, starting with אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Woe over those who are lost' is a sigh over the אבות, who are gone and cannot be replaced. Unlike משה, who asked for God's name and complained, the אבות accepted His ways even when things looked unfair.

keyTerms.meaning: woe over those who are lost
God Almighty, the name by which God appeared to the אבות

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
Woe over those who are lost and are no longer found.
For several times I revealed Myself

phrases.aramaic: עַל אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב בְּאֵל שַׁדַּי,
phrases.english: to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as אל שדי,
and they did not question My ways,
and they did not say to Me, 'What is Your name?'
phrases.notes: This hints at משה, who did ask God's name at the burning bush.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: חֲבָל עַל דְּאָבְדִין וְלָא מִשְׁתַּכְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives הקדוש ברוך הוא's response to משה's complaint from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אבות trusted הקדוש ברוך הוא completely and never questioned His ways, unlike משה.

steps.title: אברהם paid for a grave in his own promised land
steps.stepSummary: The first example: אברהם was promised the whole land, yet he had to pay 400 silver shekels to bury שרה, and he still did not complain.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to אברהם: 'Arise, walk through the land, its length and its width, for I will give it to you.' He looked for a place to bury שרה and did not find one until he bought it for four hundred silver shekels, and he did not question My ways.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא proves His point about the אבות with a story about אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was promised the entire land, yet he could not even find a grave for שרה without paying a high price. That looked like a broken promise, but he never complained. This is exactly the trust משה failed to show.

phrases.english: I said to Abraham: 'Arise, walk through the land'
'its length and its width, for to you I will give it.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:17

phrases.aramaic: בִּקֵּשׁ מָקוֹם לִקְבּוֹר אֶת שָׂרָה וְלֹא מָצָא,
phrases.english: He looked for a place to bury Sarah and did not find one,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁקָּנָה בְּאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: until he bought it for four hundred silver shekels,
and he did not question My ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first example proving the claim of step 18 that the אבות never questioned God.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the אבות did not question הקדוש ברוך הוא's ways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אברהם was promised the whole land, yet he paid 400 silver shekels for a grave for שרה without complaining.

steps.title: Second example: יצחק fought over water and did not complain
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ promised יצחק blessing in the land, yet his servants had to fight over water. יצחק still did not question ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: I told יצחק: 'Live in this land, I will be with you and bless you.' Yet his servants could not find water to drink until they had to fight over it, as the פסוק says the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with יצחק's shepherds over the water. Still, he did not question My ways.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ continues His list of the אבות. After אברהם, He now gives יצחק as a second example of someone who stayed faithful even when the promise seemed far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as with אברהם: a big promise is followed by a hard reality. יצחק was promised blessing, but he could not even get water without a fight. Even so, he did not complain.

keyTerms.meaning: Questioned My ways (doubted how ה׳ acts)

phrases.english: I said to Isaac:
"Sojourn in this land,
phrases.notes: בראשית 26:3

phrases.english: and I will be with you and will bless you."
His servants looked for water to drink
and did not find it, until they had a quarrel,
as it is stated: "And the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled

phrases.aramaic: עִם רֹעֵי יִצְחָק לֵאמֹר לָנוּ הַמָּיִם״.
phrases.english: with Isaac's herdsmen, saying: The water is ours."
phrases.notes: בראשית 26:20

phrases.english: And he did not question My ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second example in the list that began with אברהם in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The claim from step 18 that the אבות never questioned ה׳'s ways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 26:3 and 26:20: the promise to יצחק and the fight over water.

steps.title: Third example: יעקב had to buy land and did not complain
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ promised יעקב the land he lay on, yet he had to buy a spot for his tent for a hundred coins. He still did not question ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: I told יעקב: 'The land you are lying on, I will give to you.' Yet he looked for a place to set up his tent and could not find one until he bought it for a hundred coins. Still, he did not question My ways.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ gives the third and last example, יעקב. Like his father and grandfather, he was promised the land but had to pay for a small piece of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the pattern of three: אברהם paid for a grave, יצחק fought for water, and יעקב paid for a place to camp. All three accepted it quietly. This sets up the contrast with משה in the next step.

phrases.english: I said to Jacob:
"The land on which you lie,
to you I will give it."
phrases.notes: בראשית 28:13

phrases.english: He looked for a place to pitch his tent,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מָצָא, עַד שֶׁקָּנָה בְּמֵאָה קְשִׂיטָה,
phrases.english: and did not find one, until he bought it for a hundred coins,
phrases.notes: This is the purchase in בראשית 33:19.

phrases.english: and he did not question My ways,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final example of an אב who did not complain.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the אבות never questioned ה׳'s ways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 28:13 and the purchase of land for a hundred קשיטה.

steps.title: The contrast: the אבות never asked, but משה asked and complained
steps.stepSummary: The אבות never asked ה׳ His name. משה asked 'What is Your name?' at the very start, and now complains that ה׳ has not saved the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they never said to Me, 'What is Your name?' But you asked Me 'What is Your name?' right at the beginning, and now you say to Me, 'You have not saved Your people.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the three examples, ה׳ turns to משה and makes the point of the whole speech. The אבות trusted Him without asking, but משה questioned Him twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to step 18, where we learned the אבות did not ask His name. משה failed in two ways: he asked for ה׳'s name at the burning bush, and after things got worse in מצרים he complained that ה׳ had not saved them.

keyTerms.meaning: You have not saved at all

steps.whatToRemember: The three אבות were promised the land, faced hardship, and never complained. משה questioned ה׳, and that is why he is criticized.

phrases.english: and they did not say to Me: "What is Your name?"
And you said to Me: "What is Your name?" at the very start,
phrases.notes: This is at the burning bush, שמות 3:13.

phrases.english: and now you say to Me:
"Neither have You saved Your people."
phrases.notes: שמות 5:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the three examples to draw the contrast with משה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unlike the אבות, משה questioned ה׳, and that is the complaint step 17 said he was punished for.

steps.title: משה's punishment: he will see פרעה fall but not the conquest of the land
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'now' in 'Now you will see what I will do to פרעה', the גמרא learns that משה will see only the war with פרעה, not the war against the thirty-one kings of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Now you will see what I will do to פרעה.' This means: the war with פרעה you will see, but the war with the thirty-one kings you will not see.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads ה׳'s reply to משה's complaint and finds the punishment hidden in it. משה will not live to lead the people into ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עתה ('now') is read as a limit: only what happens now, with פרעה. The later conquest of the land under יהושע is left out. This is the punishment step 17 mentioned.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself does not say משה will not enter the land. The גמרא learns it from the word 'now', which suggests 'only this, not later.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It links משה's not entering ארץ ישראל to his complaint here in מצרים, not only to the later story of the rock.

phrases.english: "Now you will see
what I will do to Pharaoh."
phrases.notes: שמות 6:1

phrases.english: The war with Pharaoh you will see,
but you will not see
the war with the thirty-one kings.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַתָּה תִרְאֶה אֵת אֲשֶׁר אֶעֱשֶׂה לְפַרְעֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the punishment for the complaint described in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of his complaint, משה would see פרעה's downfall but would not lead the conquest of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: What did משה see that made him bow quickly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where משה hurried to bow after ה׳ revealed His attributes, and asks what he saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And משה hurried, bowed to the ground, and prostrated himself.' What did משה see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks which of ה׳'s attributes made משה rush to bow, and this sets up the opinions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'hurried' suggests that משה saw something specific that made him act right away. The גמרא wants to know which attribute from the list in שמות 34 caused it.

phrases.english: "And Moses hurried, and bowed his head to the ground, and prostrated himself."
phrases.notes: שמות 34:8, right after ה׳ calls out His attributes (the י״ג מדות).

phrases.english: What did Moses see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about משה and how ה׳ deals with people.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which attribute caused משה to hurry and bow.

steps.title: Two answers: patience or truth
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן גמלא says משה saw ארך אפים (slow to anger). The רבנן say he saw אמת (truth).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמלא says: he saw 'slow to anger.' The רבנן say: he saw 'truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two opinions answer the question from step 24. Each one picks a different attribute that moved משה to bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers come from the same list of attributes in the פסוקים. The argument is over which one struck משה most: ה׳'s patience, or His truth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamla says:
He saw "slow to anger,"
and the Rabbis say: He saw "truth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either ארך אפים (רבי חנינא בן גמלא) or אמת (רבנן).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports ארך אפים: משה said the wicked should be lost
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that משה found ה׳ writing 'slow to anger.' משה said it should apply only to the righteous and that the wicked should be lost. ה׳ told him he would one day need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports the view that he saw 'slow to anger.' When משה went up on high, he found ה׳ sitting and writing 'slow to anger.' משה said: 'Master of the world, slow to anger for the righteous?' ה׳ said: 'Even for the wicked.' משה said: 'Let the wicked be lost!' ה׳ said: 'Now you will see that you will need it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי חנינא בן גמלא. The story shows that ארך אפים was already something משה had discussed with ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה at first thought patience was only for the righteous. ה׳ hinted that משה himself would later need patience for sinners. So when it was revealed again, משה hurried to bow. The story continues, and its ending will show how the hint came true.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with the one who said

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with the one who said
he saw "slow to anger,"
as it is taught: When Moses went up on high,
he found the Holy One, Blessed be He,
sitting and writing "slow to anger."
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
"slow to anger" for the righteous?
He said to him: "Even for the wicked."
He said to Him: Let the wicked be lost!
He said to him: Now you will see
that you will need it.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets (מאי, 'what') and some don't. The meaning is the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם רָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first opinion in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא בן גמלא's view that משה saw ארך אפים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about משה finding ה׳ writing ארך אפים and arguing that it should not apply to the wicked.

steps.title: ה׳ turns משה's words back to him when ישראל sin
steps.stepSummary: When ישראל sinned, ה׳ asked משה: didn't you tell Me that ארך אפים is only for the צדיקים?
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Jewish people sinned, ה׳ said to משה: Didn't you tell Me that 'slow to anger' is only for the righteous?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps telling its story. ישראל have now sinned, and ה׳ reminds משה of what he said earlier. משה's answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, משה said that ארך אפים should apply only to צדיקים and that the wicked should be lost. Now ישראל themselves are the sinners, so by משה's own rule they would get no patience. ה׳'s earlier warning, that משה would one day need this, is coming true.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't you say this to Me? It reminds someone of their own words.

steps.confusionAlert: ה׳ is not really changing His mind about being patient. He is reminding משה of משה's own earlier claim, to show why משה needs ארך אפים for sinners too.

phrases.english: When the Jewish people sinned,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא כָּךְ אָמַרְתָּ לִי
phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't you say this to Me,
phrases.notes: ה׳ is the one speaking here, and He is talking to משה.

phrases.english: 'Slow to anger is for the righteous'?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁחָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא כָּךְ אָמַרְתָּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 26. ה׳'s warning that משה would need ארך אפים now comes true.
steps.raayaObject: The view that משה saw ארך אפים when he bowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuing ברייתא about משה finding ה׳ writing 'slow to anger.'
